title: Credit Builder Accounts Returned-Payment Fee and the Account's Return History
content:
The returned-payment fee on a Credit Builder account is reduced when the account has few other returned payments. "This one" is the account's most recent returned payment, the one the fee is charged for; the others are the account's remaining returned-payment entries, whatever their code, by their dates.

## Return history shares

- When no payment on the account other than this one was returned in the 12 whole calendar months before today (a return dated today counts, and one dated on the same day of the month 12 months earlier falls outside them), the fee is multiplied by the first-return share of 0.5.
- When exactly one other payment on the account was returned in those 12 months, the fee is multiplied by the second-return share of 0.75.
- When two or more other payments on the account were returned in those 12 months, the fee is not reduced for return history (a share of 1.0).

The share multiplies the fee before it is rounded to the cent.

| Other payments returned in the 12 months | Share |
|---|---|
| none | 0.5 |
| exactly one | 0.75 |
| two or more | no reduction |

## Edge of the 12 months (hypothetical dates)

Today 12 July: another return dated 12 July of the previous year falls outside the 12 months; one dated 13 July of the previous year is counted; one dated today is counted.
